3869.t: Beekes attributes it to a Mediterranean substrate, probably Pre-Greek.

3884.t: A zero-grade formation from or closely related to λιμήν (limḗn, “harbor”) and λειμών (leimṓn, “moist place, meadow”).

3888.t: From Proto-Hellenic *məňňómai, from Proto-Indo-European *mn̥yétor (“to think”), from *men-. Cognates include Sanskrit मन्य॑ते (mányate), Old Church Slavonic мьнѣти (mĭněti), Old Irish ·muinethar, and Lithuanian miniu.

3875.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kéntron, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱéntrom, from *ḱent- (“to prick; point”); direct cognate with Albanian çandër (“forked pole”) and probably Old Armenian սանտր (santr), սանդր (sandr, “comb”).

3882.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-ti Proto-Indo-European *léyǵʰti Proto-Hellenic *léikʰō Ancient Greek λείχω From Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ-.

3885.t: Uncertain. First attested as Mycenaean Greek 𐀪𐀜 (ri-no), could be from Proto-Indo-European *linom, with cognates including Old Church Slavonic льнъ (lĭnŭ), Latin līnum, and Gothic 𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌽 (lein).

3843.t: An Elamite origin has been suggested but, according to Beekes, the group σσ/ττ (ss/tt) is typically Pre-Greek, so the word would have come from Greece or Western Anatolia, like μόλυβδος (mólubdos, “lead”), but even if so, the word might still go back to…

3841.t: Directly from τίθημι (títhēmi, “to put, place”) + -σις (-sis). Although, it could either have been formed in Greek, or Proto-Indo-European.

3822.t: For *δϝέϳος (*dwéjos), the σ-stem abstract noun formed from Proto-Indo-European *dwey- (“to fear”), whence also δεινός (deinós). Cognate to Old Armenian երկն (erkn), Latin dīrus.

3838.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰh₁-dʰmó-s, from *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put, place”). Cognate with Welsh deddf (“act, statute”).

3897.t: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *mānúō, from Proto-Indo-European *mh₂néwti, a nu-infix formation to *(s)meh₂- (“to beckon”).

3876.t: Attested in Mycenaean Greek 𐀑𐀺 (ki-wo). From Proto-Indo-European *ḱiHwon-, whence also Old Armenian սիւն (siwn, “column; pillar”).

3840.t: Uncertain. Often connected to such forms as θαῦμα (thaûma, “wonder, marvel”), θώψ (thṓps, “flatterer, false friend”), τάφος (táphos, “amazement”) and τέθηπα (téthēpa, “to be astonished”).

3868.t: Unknown. Traditionally analyzed as an old compound of κάρα (kárā, “head”) (in the form κράσ-), with a faded second member πέδον (pédon, “plain, ground”), for which Sanskrit द्रुपद (drupada, “wooden pillar, post”) is compared.

3858.t: From κατήγορος (kătḗgoros) + -έω (-éō), or from κατα- (kătă-, “against”) + ἀγορεύω (agoreúō, “to speak in assembly”).

3887.t: From μακρόθυμος (măkróthūmos, “long-suffering, patient”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from μακρο- (makro-, “long”) + θυμός (thūmós, “soul; temper, passion”).

3873.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂emp-, an extension of *kh₂em- (“to bend, curve”), and thus related to κάμπτω (kámptō, “to curve”). Alternatively, compare Sanskrit कपना (kapanā́, “caterpillar”), Latvian kâpe (“insect larva”).

3874.t: Uncertain. * Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *k(e)rt- (“to turn”), related to Ancient Greek κυρτία (kurtía, “anything made of wicker”), Sanskrit कृणत्ति (kṛṇátti, “to twist thread, to spin”), Sanskrit चृटति (cṛṭáti, “to bind, to fasten together”), Latin…

3883.t: Probably of Pre-Greek origin, as suggested by the suffix -ανον. The denominative simplex λαχαίνω (lakhaínō, “to dig”), which has only late attestations, is probably a back-formation from compounded forms.

3865.t: Based on the suffix, frequent in plant names of substrate origin, Beekes takes the word as Pre-Greek.

3886.t: From the same root as λιτός (lĭtós, “supplicatory”) and λιτή (lĭtḗ, “prayer, entreaty”), said root of unknown origin, but the fact that the λ (l) often makes a preceding short vowel into a heavy syllable, as well as the frequent doubling of the λ (l) after…

3835.t: Sommer connected the word with ζῆλος (zêlos, “fervour, zeal”), ζητέω (zētéō, “to inquire, search, investigate”), and δίζημαι (dízēmai, “to seek out, look for”), based on a breakdown of the word as ζη-μία (zē-mía), which suggests a derivation from…

3871.t: A secondary present form of κυλίνδω (kŭlíndō, “to roll, turn over”).
